newsitem.title: INDIA: India's MOIL expects a 917.2 mln turnover in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: India's MOIL expects a 917.2 mln turnover in 96/97.

text.p: India's state-owned Manganese Ore Ltd (MOIL) said on Tuesday that it expected to produce 650,000 tonnes of manganese ore and 600 tonnes of electrolytic manganese dioxide (EMD) by the end of the year 1996/97.
The company said in a statement that it envisaged a net profit of 82.5 million rupees ($2.29million) on a turnover of 917.2 million ($25.48million) for the fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).

The company meets about 65 percent of the demand for high grade ore from the ferromanganese industry. It also produces EMD used to manufacture dry cells and is a major supplier of blast furnace grade ore to the steel plants.
MOIL is set to diversify and modernise in various sectors.

"As a part of diversification the company is setting up a Ferro Manganese plant of 10,000 TPA at its Balaghat mine," the company said in a statement. Balaghat is located about 350 kms southeast of Bhopal, the capital of Madhya Pradesh state.
On Tuesday, MOIL signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the government to supply manganese for the year 1996/97.

As part of economic reforms launched in 1991, the federal government has evolved a system of fixing targets for state-run firms by signing agreements, or Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs), with them, to give managements a measure of autonomy.
